periods.RahuKalam.name: Rahu Kalam
periods.RahuKalam.meaning: A daily period associated with Rahu that is traditionally considered unfavorable for beginning important or auspicious activities. Its timing is calculated using the local sunrise, sunset, and weekday.
periods.RahuKalam.description: A traditionally unfavorable period for important new beginnings.

periods.Yamagandam.name: Yamagandam
periods.Yamagandam.meaning: A daily period associated with Yama that is traditionally considered unfavorable for beginning auspicious activities. It is calculated from the local sunrise, sunset, and weekday.
periods.Yamagandam.description: A period traditionally avoided when starting important or auspicious activities.

periods.DurMuhurtam.name: Dur Muhurtam
periods.DurMuhurtam.meaning: A period of the day considered unfavorable when selecting an auspicious Muhurta. Depending on the weekday, there may be more than one Dur Muhurtam period.
periods.DurMuhurtam.description: An unfavorable Muhurta traditionally avoided for important beginnings.

periods.GulikaKalam.name: Gulika Kalam
periods.GulikaKalam.meaning: A daily period associated with Gulika and traditionally linked with Saturn. It is generally treated with caution when choosing an auspicious starting time.
periods.GulikaKalam.description: A period traditionally treated with caution for auspicious new beginnings.

periods.Varjyam.name: Varjyam
periods.Varjyam.meaning: A Nakshatra-based period traditionally considered unsuitable for auspicious beginnings. Unlike Rahu Kalam, its timing is derived from the day's Nakshatra and may occur during the day or night.
periods.Varjyam.description: A Nakshatra-based period traditionally considered unfavorable for auspicious beginnings.

periods.BrahmaMuhurta.name: Brahma Muhurta
periods.BrahmaMuhurta.meaning: A special period before sunrise traditionally regarded as ideal for meditation, prayer, yoga, study, reflection, and spiritual practices.
periods.BrahmaMuhurta.description: A peaceful pre-sunrise period considered ideal for meditation, prayer, and spiritual practice.

periods.AbhijitMuhurta.name: Abhijit Muhurta
periods.AbhijitMuhurta.meaning: An auspicious period occurring around local midday. It is traditionally regarded as a favorable time for beginning many important activities.
periods.AbhijitMuhurta.description: An auspicious midday period considered favorable for important new beginnings.

periods.AmritKalam.name: Amrit Kalam
periods.AmritKalam.meaning: A highly auspicious period derived from Nakshatra-based calculations and traditionally associated with favorable energy and positive beginnings.
periods.AmritKalam.description: A highly auspicious period considered favorable for important and positive activities.

periods.ChoghadiyaAmrit.name: Amrit
periods.ChoghadiyaAmrit.meaning: The most auspicious Choghadiya, traditionally considered suitable for all kinds of activities.
periods.ChoghadiyaAmrit.description: The most auspicious Choghadiya, suitable for all activities.

periods.ChoghadiyaShubh.name: Shubh
periods.ChoghadiyaShubh.meaning: An auspicious Choghadiya traditionally favored for ceremonies, marriages, education and religious activities.
periods.ChoghadiyaShubh.description: An auspicious Choghadiya for ceremonies and religious activities.

periods.ChoghadiyaLabh.name: Labh
periods.ChoghadiyaLabh.meaning: A favorable Choghadiya traditionally associated with gain, and favored for business, trade, education and new ventures.
periods.ChoghadiyaLabh.description: A favorable Choghadiya for business, trade and new ventures.

periods.ChoghadiyaChal.name: Chal
periods.ChoghadiyaChal.meaning: A neutral Choghadiya traditionally considered suitable for travel and routine activities.
periods.ChoghadiyaChal.description: A neutral Choghadiya suitable for travel and routine work.
periods.ChoghadiyaChal.message: Suitable for travel and routine work

periods.ChoghadiyaUdveg.name: Udveg
periods.ChoghadiyaUdveg.meaning: An unfavorable Choghadiya traditionally avoided for new beginnings, though associated with government-related work.
periods.ChoghadiyaUdveg.description: An unfavorable Choghadiya traditionally avoided for new beginnings.

periods.ChoghadiyaKaal.name: Kaal
periods.ChoghadiyaKaal.meaning: An inauspicious Choghadiya traditionally avoided for auspicious activities.
periods.ChoghadiyaKaal.description: An inauspicious Choghadiya traditionally avoided for auspicious activities.

periods.ChoghadiyaRog.name: Rog
periods.ChoghadiyaRog.meaning: An inauspicious Choghadiya traditionally associated with illness and disputes and avoided for important activities.
periods.ChoghadiyaRog.description: An inauspicious Choghadiya traditionally avoided for important activities.

elements.tithi.name: Tithi
elements.tithi.meaning: The lunar day. Each Tithi corresponds to 12° of separation between the Moon and the Sun, giving 30 Tithis in a lunar month: 15 in the waxing (Shukla) fortnight and 15 in the waning (Krishna) fortnight. A Tithi can begin at any time of day and lasts roughly 19 to 26 hours.
elements.tithi.description: The lunar day, based on the angle between the Moon and the Sun.

elements.nakshatra.name: Nakshatra
elements.nakshatra.meaning: One of the 27 lunar mansions, each spanning 13°20′ of the sidereal zodiac. The day's Nakshatra is the one the Moon is passing through; it changes about once a day.
elements.nakshatra.description: The lunar mansion the Moon is passing through.

elements.yoga.name: Yoga
elements.yoga.meaning: One of 27 combinations obtained by adding the sidereal longitudes of the Sun and the Moon and dividing by 13°20′. Each Yoga is traditionally associated with a favorable or unfavorable quality.
elements.yoga.description: A daily combination of the Sun's and the Moon's positions.

elements.karana.name: Karana
elements.karana.meaning: Half of a Tithi, corresponding to 6° of Moon–Sun separation. There are 11 Karanas: 7 that repeat through the lunar month and 4 fixed ones. Vishti (Bhadra) is traditionally avoided for auspicious activities.

terms.sunrise.name: Sunrise
terms.sunrise.meaning: The moment the upper edge of the Sun appears on the horizon at the location, allowing for atmospheric refraction. The Panchang day begins at sunrise, and Rahu Kalam, the Muhurtas and other periods are measured from it.
terms.sunrise.description: The start of the Panchang day at this location.

terms.sunset.name: Sunset
terms.sunset.meaning: The moment the upper edge of the Sun disappears below the horizon at the location. Daytime periods such as Rahu Kalam divide the time between sunrise and sunset.
terms.sunset.description: The end of daytime at this location.

terms.vara.name: Vara
terms.vara.meaning: The weekday. In the Panchang a weekday runs from one sunrise to the next, and several daily periods, including Rahu Kalam, Yamagandam and Gulika Kalam, depend on it.
terms.vara.description: The day of the week, counted from sunrise.

terms.choghadiya.name: Choghadiya
terms.choghadiya.meaning: A system, popular in northern and western India, that divides the daytime (sunrise to sunset) and the night (sunset to next sunrise) into eight segments each. Each segment is one of Amrit, Shubh, Labh, Chal, Udveg, Kaal or Rog, in an order set by the weekday, and is used to choose favorable times for daily activities.
terms.choghadiya.description: Eight day and eight night segments used to choose favorable times.

panchangTraditions.all.description: Every timing the app calculates, including Choghadiya.

panchangTraditions.telugu.description: Varjyam, Durmuhurtham, Rahu Kalam, Yamagandam and Gulika, with Amrita Kalam, Abhijit Muhurtham and Brahma Muhurtham.

panchangTraditions.tamil.description: Rahu Kalam, Yamagandam and Kuligai, with Amirtha Kalam, Abhijit Muhurtham and Brahma Muhurtham.

panchangTraditions.kannada.description: Rahu Kalam, Yamagandam, Gulika and Durmuhurtha, with Amrita Kala, Abhijit Muhurtha and Brahma Muhurtha.

panchangTraditions.malayalam.description: Rahu Kalam, Yamagandam and Gulika, with Amrutha Kalam, Abhijit Muhurtham and Brahma Muhurtham.

panchangTraditions.north-indian.description: Rahu Kaal, Choghadiya and Abhijit Muhurat, with Amrit Kaal and Brahma Muhurat.

panchangTraditions.gujarati.description: Choghadiya, Rahu Kaal and Abhijit Muhurat, with Amrit Kaal and Brahma Muhurat.

panchangTraditions.marathi.description: Rahu Kaal, Abhijit Muhurat and Choghadiya, with Amrit Kaal and Brahma Muhurat.

guidanceRatings.HighlyFavorable.name: Highly Favorable
guidanceRatings.HighlyFavorable.description: Today's Panchang factors are strongly supportive for common activities.

guidanceRatings.Favorable.name: Favorable
guidanceRatings.Favorable.description: Today's Panchang factors are generally supportive for common activities.

guidanceRatings.Mixed.name: Mixed
guidanceRatings.Mixed.description: Today's Panchang factors are mixed; choose timings carefully for important activities.

guidanceRatings.Caution.name: Caution
guidanceRatings.Caution.description: Several of today's Panchang factors call for caution; prefer the recommended time periods for important activities.

guidanceRatings.Avoid.name: Traditionally Avoided
guidanceRatings.Avoid.description: Today's Panchang factors are traditionally considered unfavorable for new beginnings.

guidanceText.check.message: Check the recommended and traditionally avoided time periods below before beginning an important activity.

guidanceText.mixed.message: Mixed, where favorable and unfavorable periods overlap: {windows}.

guidanceText.methodology.name: Daily guidance
guidanceText.methodology.description: Daily guidance summarizes the five Panchanga limbs (Tithi, Vara, Nakshatra, Yoga, Karana) using this app's methodology. It is not a universal traditional rule and not a Muhurta for a specific ceremony such as a marriage or housewarming.

guidanceGroups.tithi.nanda.description: Nanda Tithi (1st, 6th, 11th), traditionally associated with joy.

guidanceGroups.tithi.bhadra.description: Bhadra Tithi (2nd, 7th, 12th), traditionally good for steady, auspicious work.

guidanceGroups.tithi.jaya.description: Jaya Tithi (3rd, 8th, 13th), traditionally associated with success.

guidanceGroups.tithi.rikta.description: Rikta Tithi (4th, 9th, 14th), traditionally avoided for new beginnings.

guidanceGroups.tithi.purna.description: Purna Tithi (5th, 10th, full moon), traditionally considered complete and auspicious.

guidanceGroups.tithi.ashtami.description: Ashtami, traditionally treated with caution for new beginnings.

guidanceGroups.tithi.amavasya.description: New moon, traditionally avoided for auspicious beginnings and observed for ancestral rites.

guidanceGroups.tithi.waning.description: A waning-Moon Tithi, generally considered less supportive than its waxing counterpart.

guidanceGroups.nakshatra.dhruva.description: A fixed (Dhruva) Nakshatra, traditionally good for lasting undertakings.

guidanceGroups.nakshatra.mridu.description: A soft (Mridu) Nakshatra, traditionally good for gentle and creative activities.

guidanceGroups.nakshatra.kshipra.description: A swift (Kshipra) Nakshatra, traditionally good for quick and practical activities.

guidanceGroups.nakshatra.chara.description: A movable (Chara) Nakshatra, traditionally good for travel and change.

guidanceGroups.nakshatra.mishra.description: A mixed (Mishra) Nakshatra, traditionally suited only to routine activities.

guidanceGroups.nakshatra.ugra.description: A fierce (Ugra) Nakshatra, traditionally treated with caution for auspicious beginnings.

guidanceGroups.nakshatra.tikshna.description: A sharp (Tikshna) Nakshatra, traditionally avoided for auspicious beginnings.

guidanceGroups.yoga.ashubha.description: One of the malefic Yogas, traditionally treated with caution.

guidanceGroups.yoga.mahaDosha.description: Vyatipata or Vaidhriti, traditionally avoided for auspicious beginnings.

guidanceGroups.karana.kimstughna.description: Kimstughna, a fixed Karana traditionally considered auspicious.

guidanceGroups.karana.sthira.description: A fixed Karana (Shakuni, Chatushpada, Naga), traditionally treated with caution.

guidanceGroups.karana.bhadra.description: Vishti (Bhadra) Karana, traditionally avoided for auspicious beginnings.

guidanceGroups.vara.saumya.description: A gentle (Saumya) weekday, traditionally supportive of auspicious work.

guidanceGroups.vara.krura.description: A harsh (Krura) weekday, traditionally treated with caution for auspicious beginnings.

guidanceGroups.vara.surya.description: Sunday, traditionally suited to matters of authority and health; mixed for general auspicious work.
